speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development in the last five years (a) how many cases of child abuse and elder abuse respectively have been reported annually; (b) what are the common types of abuse inflicted on these children and elderly victims; and (c) what are the common types of familial relationship the perpetrators have with the victims.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF will continue to work closely with families and community partners to keep individuals safe.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One child or one elderly victim is one too many.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At this point in time, what is the extent of the effects of such abuse on, especially the young children or even the elderly victims that are held by MSF and their partners?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And have the victims been able to recover from the abuse and have they managed to resume normalcy in their lives after intervention by MSF and its partners?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And my second question is: how effectively have our public campaigns been in raising awareness about familial abuse, whether to children, the elderly or even to spouses, particularly in helping the general public raise the alarm on any forms of familial abuse they know of in any family that they are aware of?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We all feel for the victims and, in such cases, the effects are not only on the victims.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The effects also go on to the carers and the perpetrators themselves.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we look at it from a very serious perspective of how we can help the recovery stage and, at the same time, we want to focus on prevention.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we have not only been looking at how we can engage the victims.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also engage the perpetrators and the carers to see, when the situation is better, really how the family can move forward along those lines.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And I am very thankful to fellow Singaporeans for responding well to our campaigns, to our calls to break the silence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Because at the end of the day, it is not only about the family alone.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I think we have to play a part.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And many Singaporeans have come forward, including the family members.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For example, I received a message from one Singaporean who shared that one of her children has this issue and it is not only about that child.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is about the issue of intergenerational family violence that had been experienced by the great-grandfather, to the grandfather and down the line until today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, I am very happy that because of this awareness campaign, we realise that more of them are thinking, coming forward and we have been able to help many Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As such, we see more and more people being aware, looking out for one another.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And also, we have been training our stakeholders, educators, healthcare professionals, counsellors, as well as social workers, to sharpen their tools and how they can respond and engage those who are affected by it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We engage with community whereby we go down to the heartlands to engage heartlanders, residential homes, tertiary institutions and schools, to see how we can better engage them, equip them with the necessary tools to see how they can play a part.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we will continue to do more and we feel that it is each and everyone's responsibility to play a part so that we can take care of our children and also ensure that our elderly can grow and have graceful senior years in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I would just like to know whether, for the past three years, is the trend upwards or downwards, in terms of the number of cases being reported?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Has it been increasing for the past years or reducing?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Because of our effort to increase the awareness and also sharpen the tools with regard to those who are involved in this area, people are able to identify cases easily and bring forward anything they find not right with regard to how the victims are responding.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Nevertheless, we want to make sure that, as a whole, while we increase the awareness, we also make sure that families are able to provide a better environment for their children and the elders.
